newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade very slow - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade very slow - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was very slow Wednesday following active sales late Tuesday at $63.00 per cwt, feedlot sources said.

About 400 steers and heifers sold in Kansas at $63.00 on a live basis, with $99.00 paid on a carcass basis, they said. The sales brought weekly movement near 78,000 head, with about 31 percent contracted or formulated, USDA statistics showed.
Other bids during the day at $62.00 were passed by owners who still had cattle to sell at $63.00, they said.
No sales were reported after midday in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area.

Weekly movement in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area was estimated near 93,000 head, which included 24,800 formulated and 200 previously contracted cattle to be shipped this week, according to USDA statisitcs.

Fed cattle prices next week were seen pressured by light demand from packers because of a short work week as the industry winds down going into the Friday U.S. Independence Day holiday, market sources said.
Prices also were pressured by the need for feedlots to remain current amid outlooks for increased market-ready cattle supplies this summer, they said.
